recent_posts.title: Why cheaper AI leads to more AI usage not less
recent_posts.summary: As AI inference costs drop, developers don't reduce usage — they embed more intelligence into their products. Cheaper models lead to longer-running agents, richer user experiences, and ultimately higher demand. The economic dynamic is counterintuitive: lower cost per unit drives greater total consumption, not less, because better AI directly translates to better user experiences and more revenue.

recent_posts.title: Baseten CEO Tuhin Srivastava on Custom Models, and Building the Inference Cloud
AI Replacing Jobs is the Wrong Narrative
The One Constant in Software
recent_posts.summary: SAP's CEO reflects on the company's origins, tracing how SAP founders at IBM noticed the inefficiency of repeatedly implementing finance systems for each customer and built a scalable solution. The core insight is that while technology has evolved from mainframes to client-server, internet, mobile, and now AI, the fundamental customer need — achieving business outcomes — has remained constant. SAP is now re-engineering its entire system around AI to help enterprises do more.

recent_posts.title: SAP: Bringing the ‘Operating System’ of a Company into the AI Era with CTO Philipp Herzig
recent_posts.summary: SAP CTO Philipp Herzig discusses how SAP is integrating AI into its enterprise platform across three layers: generative UI replacing traditional click-through interfaces, AI agents automating business processes like order-to-cash, and a unified data layer. He explains why LLMs alone are insufficient for predictive analytics in enterprise settings, introducing SAP's RPT1 (Relational Pre-trained Transformers) for tabular/structured data predictions. Key challenges include scaling AI to 20,000 APIs, managing disaggregated enterprise data, and building reliable evals for business outcomes. He also covers SAP's shift from seat-based to hybrid consumption-based pricing, the concept of 'agent mining' to capture tribal knowledge, and why enterprise AI adoption lags behind the innovation curve.

recent_posts.title: ServiceNow acquires Armis to unify IT and OT security in one AI platform
recent_posts.summary: ServiceNow's acquisition of Armis aims to unify IT and OT (operational technology) security management into a single AI-powered platform. The pitch positions cybercrime as a $1 trillion/month global problem and argues that integrating asset visibility across networks, manufacturing equipment, medical devices, and critical infrastructure into one automated platform is the solution for enterprise security reinvention.

recent_posts.title: AI should serve human ambition not replace it
recent_posts.summary: A brief reflection on the rapid pace of AI-driven change and a reminder that AI should serve human ambition rather than diminish human connection and leadership. The core message is that technology must amplify human potential, not replace it.

recent_posts.title: ServiceNow says AI agents now handle 90% of customer service cases
recent_posts.summary: ServiceNow's CEO reports that AI agents now handle 90% of customer service cases, with only 10% requiring human involvement. The company expects net new headcount growth to be dramatically reduced as AI agents absorb work in finance, HR, and supporting functions that would previously have required hiring thousands of people to keep pace with company growth.

recent_posts.title: Scaling Global Organizations in the Age of AI with ServiceNow CEO Bill McDermott
recent_posts.summary: ServiceNow CEO Bill McDermott discusses enterprise AI strategy, the so-called 'SaaS apocalypse' narrative, and why replacing enterprise workflow platforms with LLMs costs 10x more. He argues that AI and enterprise platforms are complementary — AI thinks, workflow acts — and positions ServiceNow as the 'AI control tower' integrating hyperscalers, language models, and systems of record. McDermott also shares leadership lessons from his early career, the importance of human connection in the AI era, and his vision for agentic businesses where AI agents handle 90% of routine work while humans focus on judgment and relationships.

recent_posts.title: Startups vs Big AI Labs
recent_posts.summary: A startup founder argues that the key advantage startups have over big AI labs is focus and velocity. Without billions for pre-training models, startups must work backwards from customer needs to drive specific capabilities, tweaking every layer from product features to agent design to model training, rather than spreading effort across hundreds of general evaluations like large incumbents do.

top_posts.title: Karpathy argues software should be built for AI agents not humans
top_posts.summary: Andrej Karpathy argues that the software industry needs to fundamentally rethink who its customer is. Rather than building human-facing apps and UIs, companies should expose APIs directly so AI agents can interact with services on behalf of users. He illustrates this with home automation and a treadmill app, suggesting that LLMs can orchestrate complex tool calls far more flexibly than any individual app. The shift implies that agents, not humans, are becoming the primary consumers of software interfaces.

top_posts.title: Why AI Needs Blockchain
top_posts.summary: A high-level argument for why blockchain networks are uniquely suited to support AI-driven economic systems. The core thesis frames blockchains as operating systems with tamper-resistant, fully auditable compute environments — properties that become increasingly critical as AI executes tasks autonomously. Key attributes highlighted include immutable published code, transparent input/output auditability on public chains, and open-source accessibility by default.

top_posts.title: Andrej Karpathy Automated His Home
top_posts.summary: Andrej Karpathy describes building an AI agent he calls 'Dobby the elf claw' that autonomously discovered and integrated all smart home subsystems on his local network. The agent reverse-engineered APIs for Sonos speakers, lights, HVAC, shades, pool, spa, and security system, then created a dashboard and natural language interface — allowing commands like 'sleepy time' to trigger home-wide automations.

top_posts.title: Andrej Karpathy on Claude, Codex, and OpenClaw
top_posts.summary: Andrej Karpathy shares observations comparing AI coding agents, specifically praising OpenClaw (an open-source Claude-based agent) for its sophisticated memory management and compelling personality crafted through its SOUL.md document. He contrasts Claude's engaging, teammate-like personality with Codex's dry, detached interaction style, noting that many current agents fail to get personality right. He credits the creator Peter for innovating simultaneously across multiple dimensions in building OpenClaw.
